invariant: GraphvizImageBuilder initially marks a NOTE-to-non-NOTE single link as Opale-eligible. After Graphviz solves the link, SvekEdge.solve clears that flag unless DotPath#getBeziers contains at most one cubic curve. DotPath#addCurve appends one XCubicCurve2D per SVG cubic segment, so this is cubic-segment cardinality even when Graphviz reports one native spline containing several segments. EntityImageNote draws the linked Opale callout only while the solved SvekEdge remains Opale; otherwise it paints the ordinary folded note and the edge remains a separate routed link. Eligibility is therefore a property of solved cubic-curve cardinality, not merely note degree or native spline count.
causal_divergence: Rust extracts every Graphviz native spline into one flattened EdgePath.points vector and originally discarded both native-spline and cubic-segment counts. The first implementation preserved native spline count, but the rejecting top and bottom edges each contain one native spline with multiple cubic segments, so that fact remained too coarse and both callouts stayed enabled. Attached notes otherwise always call render_attached_note when an edge exists, and floating named notes do the same whenever degree-based eligibility succeeds. The note coordinates and dimensions already match after rankdir rotation; only Java's solved cubic-curve eligibility differs.
planned_change: Preserve the total cubic Bezier segment count on EdgePath by summing each native spline's `(point_count - 1) / 3`, matching DotPath#addCurve construction. Render attached and floating note callouts only when that count is at most one; otherwise use the existing ordinary folded-note renderer at the same solved node position. Propagate the new field through all EdgePath construction sites and add layout plus renderer tests. Do not infer eligibility from coordinates, source note position, fixture labels, or a numeric geometry threshold.
